item.title: Describing floodplain recovery
item.description: Describe what becomes visible when a stream can spread across its floodplain again, from seasonal waterlines and fresh layers of silt to shifting bends and new strips of riverside vegetation.

children.definition: The re-establishment of a link that lets high flows from a stream spread onto the adjoining low ground.
children.example: The first visible sign of floodplain reconnection was a sheet of shallow water spreading from the stream into a meadow that had stayed dry during previous spring rises.
children.translation_uz: daryo oʻzani bilan qayir oʻrtasidagi aloqani tiklash

children.definition: The covering of normally exposed ground by rising or spreading water.
children.example: The edge of the spring inundation was still visible after the meadow dried, marked by a line of flattened grass and stranded twigs.

children.definition: A periodic rise and fall in a river's level that temporarily brings water onto the surrounding low ground and then lets it drain away.
children.example: The spring flood pulse was visible in a series of photographs showing the meadow fill from the stream and drain until only the deepest hollows held water.
children.translation_ru: периодический подъём и спад уровня реки с затоплением и последующим осушением поймы
children.translation_uz: daryo sathi vaqti-vaqti bilan koʻtarilib, qayirni suv bosishi, soʻng sath pasaygach, suvning qayirdan chekinishi

children.definition: An abrupt switch in the course of a river when most of its flow leaves an established channel for a different route.
children.example: Photographs taken before and after the spring rise showed an avulsion at the lower end of the reconnected meadow, where most of the stream now followed a previously dry swale.
children.translation_uz: daryo oqimining keskin boshqa oʻzanga oʻtishi

children.definition: A curved lake or pool formed when a river takes a shorter course and leaves a former bend cut off from its main channel.
children.example: After the spring water receded, the oxbow stood out as a crescent of still water beyond the stream's active course.
children.translation_uz: daryoning uzilib qolgan burilishidan hosil boʻlgan koʻl

children.definition: Formed from mineral material carried and laid down by flowing water.
children.example: As the meadow dried, a pale strip of alluvial sediment marked where the spring flow had deposited fine sand and silt.

children.definition: The local removal of loose material from a channel bed or margin by a concentrated current.
children.example: Evidence of scour appeared beside a fallen trunk at the meadow inlet, where the current had hollowed out a pocket and exposed coarse gravel.
children.translation_uz: oqim taʼsirida yuz beradigan mahalliy yuvilish

children.definition: The accumulation of fine mineral particles as they settle out of water and gradually fill a channel or depression.
children.example: Siltation gradually raised the floor of a hollow in the reconnected meadow, where each spring rise left a thin layer of fine sediment.

children.definition: A strip of vegetation bordering a watercourse that filters runoff from adjoining land and provides habitat along the water's edge.
children.example: By the third summer, sedges and young willows formed a continuous riparian buffer between the stream and the mown part of the meadow.
children.translation_uz: suv oʻzani boʻyidagi himoya vazifasini bajaradigan oʻsimliklar tasmasi

children.definition: The gradual sideways or downstream movement of a river bend as the current erodes one margin and lays down sediment on the other.
children.example: Successive photographs showed meander migration into the reconnected meadow, with the outer edge of the bend retreating as fresh gravel accumulated on the inside.

children.definition: The progressive deepening of a watercourse as its current erodes the bed and cuts into the underlying material.
children.example: A remnant of the former streambed stood nearly a metre above the present bed, showing how far channel incision had lowered it before spring flows regained access to the meadow.
children.translation_uz: oqim oʻzan tubini yemirishi natijasida oʻzanning chuqurlashishi

children.definition: A raised embankment built to limit the spread of high river flows onto land beyond it.
children.example: With the new levee farther from the stream, spring water spread across the strip of meadow that the old embankment had kept dry.

children.definition: A smaller watercourse that carries a portion of a river's flow along a separate route from the main course.
children.example: During the spring rise, the secondary channel carried water around a willow-covered island before rejoining the main stream at the foot of the meadow.

children.definition: A low body of sand or gravel laid down by a river on the inner side of a bend.
children.example: When the stream fell after spreading into the reconnected meadow, a fresh layer of pale gravel was visible on the point bar inside the bend.
children.translation_ru: прирусловая отмель на внутренней стороне излучины
children.translation_uz: daryo burilishining ichki tomonida toʻplangan qum yoki shagʻal yotqizigʻi
